title: Line totals
prompt: Show each order item's order_id, product_id, and quantity times 2.5, rounded to 1 decimal, as weight.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT order_id, product_id, ROUND(quantity * 2.5, 1) AS weight FROM order_items;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT order_id, product_id, quantity AS weight FROM order_items;
SELECT order_id, product_id, ROUND(quantity + 2.5, 1) AS weight FROM order_items;

title: Short names
prompt: Show the full_name of contacts whose name has at most 8 characters.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM contacts; INSERT INTO contacts VALUES (11, 'mary jackson', 'mary-j@club.test', '555-0111', 'Hampton', 'SILVER GOLD1'), (12, 'BOB Kahn', 'bob@CLUB.test', '555-0112', NULL, 'gold1'), (13, 'Rosa Park', 'rosa@club-test', NULL, 'Tuskegee', 'NEW'), (14, 'Ken Thompson', 'ken.t@club.test', '5550114', 'Murray', 'GOLD3'); UPDATE contacts SET full_name = 'Ada Byron' WHERE id = 11; UPDATE contacts SET full_name = 'Bob Khan' WHERE id = 12;

solutions: SELECT full_name FROM contacts WHERE LENGTH(full_name) <= 8;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT full_name FROM contacts WHERE LENGTH(full_name) < 8;
SELECT full_name FROM contacts;

title: Weekend check
prompt: SQLite's strftime('%w', date) gives 0 for Sunday and 6 for Saturday. Show each session's id and a column day_type: Weekend or Weekday.
hints: Combine a date function with CASE.
solutions: SELECT id, CASE WHEN strftime('%w', session_date) IN ('0', '6') THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END AS day_type FROM sessions;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, CASE WHEN strftime('%w', session_date) IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END AS day_type FROM sessions;
SELECT id, 'Weekday' AS day_type FROM sessions;

title: Sale tags
prompt: Show each book's title and a tag named sale: the text On sale if its title contains an a or A, otherwise Regular.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM books; INSERT INTO books VALUES (10, 'Copper Moon', 'Ada Hill', 'Fantasy', 20.0, 100, 2020), (11, 'North Light', 'Raj Dev', 'Travel', 7.5, 180, 2015), (12, 'Sky Atlas', 'Ada Hill', 'Science', 25.0, 300, 2023); UPDATE books SET title = 'Blue Fog' WHERE id = 10;

solutions: SELECT title, CASE WHEN title LIKE '%a%' THEN 'On sale' ELSE 'Regular' END AS sale FROM books;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT title, CASE WHEN title LIKE 'a%' THEN 'On sale' ELSE 'Regular' END AS sale FROM books;
SELECT title, 'On sale' AS sale FROM books;

title: Pay with bonus
prompt: Show each employee's name and their salary plus bonus as total, treating a missing bonus as 0.
hints: A missing value would otherwise make the total NULL.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, salary + COALESCE(bonus, 0) AS total FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, salary + bonus AS total FROM employees;
SELECT name, salary AS total FROM employees;

title: Email domains
prompt: Everything after the @ is the domain. Show each employee's id and email domain, as domain, for employees with an email. instr(email, '@') gives the position of the @.
hints: Start SUBSTR one position after the @.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); UPDATE employees SET email = 'ivy@sub.acme.test' WHERE id = 11;

solutions: SELECT id, SUBSTR(email, instr(email, '@') + 1) AS domain FROM employees WHERE email IS NOT NULL;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, SUBSTR(email, instr(email, '@')) AS domain FROM employees WHERE email IS NOT NULL;
SELECT id, SUBSTR(email, instr(email, '@') + 1) AS domain FROM employees;

title: Month labels
prompt: Show each reading's id and a label like Mar 2024, for March 2024 readings only, as label. Use the fixed text Mar.
hints: Filter on the month, and build the label from the year.
solutions: SELECT id, 'Mar ' || strftime('%Y', reading_date) AS label FROM readings WHERE strftime('%Y-%m', reading_date) = '2024-03';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, 'Mar ' || strftime('%Y', reading_date) AS label FROM readings;
SELECT id, 'Mar' || strftime('%Y', reading_date) AS label FROM readings WHERE strftime('%Y-%m', reading_date) = '2024-03';

title: Effective discount
prompt: Show each order item's order_id, product_id, and discount, with missing discounts as 0, rounded to 1 decimal, as discount.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT order_id, product_id, ROUND(COALESCE(discount, 0), 1) AS discount FROM order_items;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT order_id, product_id, discount FROM order_items;
SELECT order_id, product_id, COALESCE(discount, 1) AS discount FROM order_items;

title: Mail merge
prompt: Show a greeting for each contact in London, as greeting: Hello, followed by a comma and space, then their name in lowercase.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM contacts; INSERT INTO contacts VALUES (11, 'mary jackson', 'mary-j@club.test', '555-0111', 'Hampton', 'SILVER GOLD1'), (12, 'BOB Kahn', 'bob@CLUB.test', '555-0112', NULL, 'gold1'), (13, 'Rosa Park', 'rosa@club-test', NULL, 'Tuskegee', 'NEW'), (14, 'Ken Thompson', 'ken.t@club.test', '5550114', 'Murray', 'GOLD3'); UPDATE contacts SET city = 'London', full_name = 'MARY J' WHERE id = 11;

solutions: SELECT 'Hello, ' || LOWER(full_name) AS greeting FROM contacts WHERE city = 'London';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT 'Hello, ' || full_name AS greeting FROM contacts WHERE city = 'London';
SELECT 'Hello, ' || LOWER(full_name) AS greeting FROM contacts;

title: Pass or fail
prompt: Show each enrolment's id and a result: Pending with no grade, Pass from 60 upwards, otherwise Fail.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT id, CASE WHEN grade IS NULL THEN 'Pending' WHEN grade >= 60 THEN 'Pass' ELSE 'Fail' END AS result FROM enrolments;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, CASE WHEN grade >= 60 THEN 'Pass' ELSE 'Fail' END AS result FROM enrolments;
SELECT id, CASE WHEN grade IS NULL THEN 'Pending' WHEN grade > 60 THEN 'Pass' ELSE 'Fail' END AS result FROM enrolments;
